import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Section conjecture

Grothendieck's section conjecture. Let $k$ be a field finitely generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let
$X$ be a complete (i.e. proper) smooth geometrically connected curve of genus at least $2$ over $k$.
Fix a geometric point $\bar{x} : \operatorname{Spec} \bar{k} \to X$ over $k$. The structure map
$X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ induces a homomorphism of profinite groups
$$p : \pi_1(X, \bar{x}) \to \pi_1(\operatorname{Spec} k) = \operatorname{Gal}(\bar{k}/k),$$
whose kernel is the geometric fundamental group $\pi_1(X \otimes_k \bar{k}, \bar{x})$.
Every rational point $x \in X(k)$ induces a splitting of $p$ (a continuous section
$\operatorname{Gal}(\bar{k}/k) \to \pi_1(X, \bar{x})$ whose image is a *decomposition group* of
$x$), well defined up to conjugation by $\pi_1(X \otimes_k \bar{k}, \bar{x})$. The section
conjecture asserts that this map from $X(k)$ to the set of
$\pi_1(X \otimes_k \bar{k}, \bar{x})$-conjugacy classes of continuous sections of $p$ is a
bijection.

## Implementation notes

Mathlib does not (yet) have the étale fundamental group of a scheme, so this file constructs the
objects appearing in the conjecture directly from Grothendieck's Galois theory:

* `FiniteEtale X` is the category of finite étale covers of `X`, and for a morphism `x : T ⟶ X`
  the functor `fiberFunctor x` sends a cover `Y ⟶ X` to the set of lifts `T ⟶ Y` of `x`. For a
  geometric point `x : Spec Ω ⟶ X` this is the fibre functor at `x`, and
  `etaleFundamentalGroup x = Aut (fiberFunctor x)` is the étale fundamental group `π₁(X, x)`, with
  its natural profinite topology (the fibres are finite sets and `Aut (fiberFunctor x)` embeds into
  the product of the discrete groups of permutations of the fibres).
* The absolute Galois group `Gal(k̄/k)` is `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k` with its Krull topology.
  It is identified with `π₁(Spec k, Spec k̄ → Spec k)` through its natural (continuous) action on
  the fibres of finite étale covers of `Spec k`; via this identification the map `p` and the
  notions "`s` is a section of `p`" (`IsSection`), "`δ` lies in the geometric fundamental group
  `π₁(X ⊗ k̄) = ker p`" (`geometricFundamentalGroup`) and "the étale path `γ` lies over the
  identity of `Gal(k̄/k)`" (`IsGeometricPath`) are expressed componentwise on the fibres of the
  covers pulled back from `Spec k`.
* A rational point `x : Spec k ⟶ X` gives the geometric point `Spec k̄ → Spec k → X`, on whose
  fibre functor `Gal(k̄/k)` acts naturally (`rationalPointSection`). The class of sections
  induced by `x` (`InducedByRationalPoint`) consists of the transports of this action along étale
  paths `γ : fiberFunctor (Spec k̄ → Spec k → X) ≅ fiberFunctor x̄` lying over the identity of
  `Gal(k̄/k)` (i.e. étale paths in `X ⊗ k̄`); this is exactly one
  `π₁(X ⊗ k̄, x̄)`-conjugacy class of sections.
* Mathlib has no notion of the genus of a curve. For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve
  over a field of characteristic zero, the genus is at least `2` if and only if the geometric
  fundamental group is non-abelian (it is trivial in genus `0`, isomorphic to `Ẑ²` in genus `1`, and
  the profinite completion of a non-abelian surface group in genus `≥ 2`); this is the form in which
  the genus hypothesis is stated.
* A field `k` of characteristic zero is finitely generated over `ℚ` (as a field) if and only if
  `Algebra.EssFiniteType ℚ k` holds (`IntermediateField.fg_top_iff`).

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Section conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* A. Grothendieck, *Brief an G. Faltings*, in *Geometric Galois actions, 1*, London Math. Soc.
  Lecture Note Ser. 242, Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 49–58.
* J. Stix, *Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics
  2054, Springer (2013).
-/

namespace SectionConjecture

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Limits Field

universe u

/- ### The étale fundamental group -/

/-- The category of finite étale covers of a scheme `X`: the full subcategory of `Over X`
consisting of the finite étale morphisms `Y ⟶ X`. -/
abbrev FiniteEtale (X : Scheme.{u}) :=
  MorphismProperty.Over (@IsFinite ⊓ @IsEtale) ⊤ X

variable {X T : Scheme.{u}}

/-- The fibre functor at a point `x : T ⟶ X`: it sends a finite étale cover `Y ⟶ X` to the set
of lifts `T ⟶ Y` of `x`. When `T = Spec Ω` for an algebraically closed field `Ω`, this is the
fibre functor of Grothendieck's Galois theory at the geometric point `x`. -/
def fiberFunctor (x : T ⟶ X) : FiniteEtale X ⥤ Type u where
  obj Y := { y : T ⟶ Y.left // (y ≫ Y.hom) = x }
  map {Y Y'} φ y := ⟨y.1 ≫ φ.left, by rw [Category.assoc, MorphismProperty.Over.w, y.2]⟩

/-- The étale fundamental group `π₁(X, x)` of `X` at the geometric point `x`: the automorphism
group of the fibre functor at `x`. -/
abbrev etaleFundamentalGroup (x : T ⟶ X) :=
  Aut (fiberFunctor x)

/-- The profinite topology on the étale fundamental group: the topology induced by the embedding
`σ ↦ (Y ↦ σ.app Y)` into the product over all covers `Y` of the sets of self-maps of the
(finite) fibre of `Y`, each carrying the discrete topology. -/
instance (x : T ⟶ X) : TopologicalSpace (etaleFundamentalGroup x) :=
  TopologicalSpace.induced (fun σ (Y : FiniteEtale X) => σ.hom.app Y)
    (@Pi.topologicalSpace _ (fun Y => (fiberFunctor x).obj Y → (fiberFunctor x).obj Y)
      fun _ => ⊥)

/- ### The absolute Galois group of `k` as `π₁(Spec k)` -/

variable (k : Type u) [Field k]

/-- The canonical morphism `Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, where `k̄ = AlgebraicClosure k`. This is the
geometric point of `Spec k` used as the base point of `π₁(Spec k)`. -/
noncomputable def closurePoint : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))

/-- The automorphism of `Spec k̄` induced by an element `g` of the absolute Galois group
`Gal(k̄/k)`. -/
noncomputable def galSpec (g : absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (g : AlgebraicClosure k ≃ₐ[k] AlgebraicClosure k).toRingHom)

/-- `galSpec` sends the identity to the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 12 14]
theorem galSpec_one : galSpec k 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
  simp only [galSpec]
  exact Spec.map_id _

/-- `g ↦ galSpec g` is compatible with multiplication, so that `g • y = galSpec g ≫ y` is a left
action of `Gal(k̄/k)` on morphisms out of `Spec k̄`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12 14]
theorem galSpec_mul (g h : absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    galSpec k (g * h) = galSpec k g ≫ galSpec k h := by
  simp only [galSpec, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
  rfl

/-- `Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k` is invariant under the Galois group. -/
@[category API, AMS 12 14]
theorem galSpec_comp_closurePoint (g : absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    (galSpec k g ≫ closurePoint k) = closurePoint k := by
  simp only [galSpec, closurePoint, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
  congr 2
  ext x
  simp

variable {k}

/- ### The homomorphism `π₁(X, x̄) → Gal(k̄/k)` and its sections -/

variable (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))

/-- Base change of finite étale covers along the structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`. -/
noncomputable abbrev baseChange : FiniteEtale (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ FiniteEtale X :=
  MorphismProperty.Over.pullback (@IsFinite ⊓ @IsEtale) ⊤ f

/-- Let `f : X ⟶ Spec k` be a `k`-scheme and `x̄ : Spec k̄ ⟶ X` a geometric point over `k`.
A continuous homomorphism `s : Gal(k̄/k) → π₁(X, x̄)` is a *section* of the natural map
`p : π₁(X, x̄) → Gal(k̄/k)` induced by `f` if `p ∘ s = id`. Under the identification of `Gal(k̄/k)`
with `π₁(Spec k)` (acting on the fibres of finite étale covers of `Spec k` through `galSpec`), this
says: for every finite étale cover `Z ⟶ Spec k` and every lift `y : Spec k̄ ⟶ Z ×_k X` of `x̄`,
the element `s g` moves `y` to a lift whose `Z`-component is `g` applied to the `Z`-component
of `y`. -/
def IsSection (ξ : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X)
    (s : absoluteGaloisGroup k →ₜ* etaleFundamentalGroup ξ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : absoluteGaloisGroup k) (Z : FiniteEtale (Spec (.of k)))
    (y : (fiberFunctor ξ).obj ((baseChange f).obj Z)),
    (((s g).hom.app _ y).1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f) = galSpec k g ≫ y.1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f

/-- The kernel `ker (π₁(X, x̄) → Gal(k̄/k))` of the natural map induced by `f`: the subgroup of
`π₁(X, x̄)` of those automorphisms of the fibre functor which act trivially on the fibres of all
covers pulled back from `Spec k`. For `X` geometrically connected over `k`, this is the geometric
fundamental group `π₁(X ⊗_k k̄, x̄)` (exactness of the fundamental sequence). -/
def geometricFundamentalGroup (ξ : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X) :
    Subgroup (etaleFundamentalGroup ξ) where
  carrier := {δ | ∀ (Z : FiniteEtale (Spec (.of k)))
    (y : (fiberFunctor ξ).obj ((baseChange f).obj Z)),
    ((δ.hom.app _ y).1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f) = y.1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f}
  one_mem' := fun _ _ => rfl
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb Z y := by
    rw [Aut.Aut_mul_def]
    change ((a.hom.app _ (b.hom.app _ y)).1 ≫ _) = _
    rw [ha, hb]
  inv_mem' {a} ha Z y := by
    rw [Aut.Aut_inv_def]
    have := ha Z (a.symm.hom.app _ y)
    have h : a.hom.app _ (a.symm.hom.app _ y) = y := congr_fun (a.inv_hom_id_app _) y
    rw [h] at this
    exact this.symm

/- ### The sections induced by a rational point -/

/-- The rational points `X(k)` of `X`, i.e. the sections `Spec k ⟶ X` of `f : X ⟶ Spec k`. -/
def RationalPoint :=
  { x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X // (x ≫ f) = 𝟙 _ }

variable {f}

/-- The natural action of `Gal(k̄/k)` on the fibre functor at the geometric point
`x̄ = closurePoint k ≫ x : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k ⟶ X` underlying a rational point `x`: the element `g`
sends a lift `y` to `galSpec g ≫ y`. This is the section of `π₁(X, x̄) → Gal(k̄/k)` induced by `x`
at the base point `x̄` (its image is the decomposition group of `x`). -/
noncomputable def rationalPointSection (x : RationalPoint f) :
    absoluteGaloisGroup k →* etaleFundamentalGroup (closurePoint k ≫ x.1) where
  toFun g :=
    { hom := { app := fun Y y => ⟨galSpec k g ≫ y.1, by
        rw [Category.assoc, y.2, ← Category.assoc, galSpec_comp_closurePoint]⟩ }
      inv := { app := fun Y y => ⟨galSpec k g⁻¹ ≫ y.1, by
        rw [Category.assoc, y.2, ← Category.assoc, galSpec_comp_closurePoint]⟩ }
      hom_inv_id := by
        ext Y y
        apply Subtype.ext
        change (galSpec k g⁻¹ ≫ galSpec k g ≫ y.1) = y.1
        rw [← Category.assoc, ← galSpec_mul, inv_mul_cancel, galSpec_one, Category.id_comp]
      inv_hom_id := by
        ext Y y
        apply Subtype.ext
        change (galSpec k g ≫ galSpec k g⁻¹ ≫ y.1) = y.1
        rw [← Category.assoc, ← galSpec_mul, mul_inv_cancel, galSpec_one, Category.id_comp] }
  map_one' := by
    ext Y y
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (galSpec k 1 ≫ y.1) = y.1
    rw [galSpec_one, Category.id_comp]
  map_mul' g h := by
    ext Y y
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (galSpec k (g * h) ≫ y.1) = galSpec k g ≫ galSpec k h ≫ y.1
    rw [galSpec_mul, Category.assoc]

variable (f) in
/-- An étale path `γ` between two geometric points `x̄₁, x̄₂ : Spec k̄ ⟶ X` over `k` (i.e. an
isomorphism of the corresponding fibre functors) *lies over the identity of* `Gal(k̄/k)` if it
induces the identity on the fibres of all covers pulled back from `Spec k`. These are exactly the
étale paths from `x̄₁` to `x̄₂` in `X ⊗_k k̄`. -/
def IsGeometricPath {ξ₁ ξ₂ : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X}
    (γ : fiberFunctor ξ₁ ≅ fiberFunctor ξ₂) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Z : FiniteEtale (Spec (.of k))) (y : (fiberFunctor ξ₁).obj ((baseChange f).obj Z)),
    ((γ.hom.app _ y).1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f) = y.1 ≫ pullback.fst Z.hom f

/-- A continuous homomorphism `s : Gal(k̄/k) → π₁(X, x̄)` is *induced by the rational point* `x`
if it is obtained from the natural action `rationalPointSection x` of `Gal(k̄/k)` on the fibre
functor at the geometric point `closurePoint k ≫ x` underlying `x` by transport along an étale
path `γ : fiberFunctor (closurePoint k ≫ x) ≅ fiberFunctor x̄` in `X ⊗_k k̄` (i.e. lying over the

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Section conjecture

Grothendieck's section conjecture. Let $k$ be a field finitely generated over $\mathbb{Q}$,
let $X$ be a complete (i.e. proper) smooth geometrically connected curve of genus at least $2$
over $k$, and let $\bar{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$. The structure map $X \to \mathrm{Spec}(k)$
induces a homomorphism of profinite groups
$$p \colon \pi_1(X, \bar{x}) \to \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{k}/k)$$
from the étale fundamental group of $X$ to the absolute Galois group of $k$.
Every rational point $x \in X(k)$ induces a continuous section of $p$ (its decomposition group),
well defined up to conjugation by the geometric fundamental group
$\pi_1(X_{\bar{k}}, \bar{x}) = \ker p$. The conjecture says that the resulting map
$$X(k) \to \{\text{continuous sections of } p\} / \pi_1(X_{\bar{k}}, \bar{x})\text{-conjugacy}$$
is a bijection.

Mathlib does not have the étale fundamental group of a scheme or the genus of a curve, so this
file defines them from scratch:

* `FiniteEtale X` is the category of finite étale schemes over `X`,
  `fiberFunctor xbar : FiniteEtale X ⥤ Type u` is the fiber functor of a geometric point
  `xbar : Spec Ω ⟶ X`, and `etaleFundamentalGroup xbar` is its automorphism group, with the
  profinite topology (the coarsest topology for which the action on each fiber is continuous).
* For a scheme `X` over `k` with a geometric point `xbar` over the canonical geometric point
  `ȷ̄ : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, the map `p : π₁(X, xbar) → Gal(k̄/k)` is encoded by the
  relation `LiesOver f η σ`: it holds when `η` acts on the fiber of every cover pulled back
  from `Spec k` in the same way as `σ ∈ Gal(k̄/k)`. In particular, `η ∈ ker p` if and only if
  `LiesOver f η 1`.
* `rationalPointSection x : Gal(k̄/k) →* π₁(X, x ∘ ȷ̄)` is the section induced by a rational
  point `x` at the tautological geometric point `x ∘ ȷ̄`, and `IsInducedBy f xbar s x` says
  that `s` is the conjugate of `rationalPointSection x` by some path (isomorphism of fiber
  functors) from `x ∘ ȷ̄` to `xbar` lying over `k`. Such paths form a torsor under
  `ker p = π₁(X_k̄, xbar)`, so the homomorphisms `s` satisfying `IsInducedBy f xbar s x` form
  exactly the `π₁(X_k̄, xbar)`-conjugacy class of the section induced by `x`.
* `genus f` is the dimension over `k` of the space of global sections of the sheaf of relative
  differentials `Ω¹_{X/k}`, realised as compatible families of Kähler differentials on the
  affine opens of `X`.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Section conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* A. Grothendieck, *Brief an G. Faltings* (letter to G. Faltings, 27 June 1983), in
  *Geometric Galois actions, 1*, London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 242, Cambridge Univ. Press,
  1997, pp. 49–58.
* J. Stix, *Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups: evidence for the section
  conjecture*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 2054, Springer, 2013.

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry

namespace SectionConjecture

universe u

section EtaleFundamentalGroup

/-- The category of finite étale schemes over `X`. -/
abbrev FiniteEtale (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type _ :=
  MorphismProperty.Over (@IsFinite ⊓ @IsEtale) ⊤ X

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : CommRingCat.{u}} (xbar : Spec Ω ⟶ X)

/-- The fiber functor of a geometric point `xbar : Spec Ω ⟶ X` (the intended use is `Ω` an
algebraically closed field): it sends a finite étale `Y ⟶ X` to the set of lifts of `xbar`
to `Y`. -/
def fiberFunctor : FiniteEtale X ⥤ Type u where
  obj Y := { y : Spec Ω ⟶ Y.left // (y ≫ Y.hom) = xbar }
  map {Y Z} g y := ⟨y.1 ≫ g.left, by rw [Category.assoc, MorphismProperty.Over.w, y.2]⟩

/-- The étale fundamental group `π₁(X, xbar)` of `X` at the geometric point `xbar`: the
automorphism group of the fiber functor. -/
abbrev etaleFundamentalGroup := Aut (fiberFunctor xbar)

/-- The profinite topology on `π₁(X, xbar)`: the topology induced by the embedding into the
product, over all finite étale `Y ⟶ X`, of the sets of self-maps of the (finite) fibers
`(fiberFunctor xbar).obj Y`, each fiber carrying the discrete topology. -/
instance : TopologicalSpace (etaleFundamentalGroup xbar) :=
  TopologicalSpace.induced
    (fun (α : etaleFundamentalGroup xbar) (Y : FiniteEtale X) (y : (fiberFunctor xbar).obj Y) =>
      α.hom.app Y y)
    (Pi.topologicalSpace (t₂ := fun _ => Pi.topologicalSpace (t₂ := fun _ => ⊥)))

end EtaleFundamentalGroup

section GaloisGroup

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- The canonical geometric point `ȷ̄ : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k` of `Spec k`, where `k̄` is the
algebraic closure of `k`. -/
noncomputable def specAlgebraicClosure (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))

/-- The automorphism of `Spec k̄` induced by an element `σ` of the absolute Galois group
`Gal(k̄/k)` of `k`. Precomposition with `galSpec σ` is a left action of `Gal(k̄/k)` on morphisms
`Spec k̄ ⟶ Y`. -/
noncomputable def galSpec (σ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    (show AlgebraicClosure k ≃ₐ[k] AlgebraicClosure k from σ).toRingEquiv.toRingHom)

/-- `galSpec σ` is an automorphism of `Spec k̄` over `Spec k`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem galSpec_comp_specAlgebraicClosure (σ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    (galSpec σ ≫ specAlgebraicClosure k) = specAlgebraicClosure k := by
  simp only [galSpec, specAlgebraicClosure, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
  congr 2
  ext x
  exact (show AlgebraicClosure k ≃ₐ[k] AlgebraicClosure k from σ).commutes x

/-- `galSpec` is compatible with multiplication: precomposition with `galSpec` is a left action. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem galSpec_mul (σ τ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    galSpec (σ * τ) = galSpec σ ≫ galSpec τ := by
  simp only [galSpec, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
  rfl

/-- `galSpec 1` is the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem galSpec_one : galSpec (1 : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) = 𝟙 _ := by
  simp only [galSpec]
  rw [← Spec.map_id]
  rfl

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))

/-- Let `xbar, xbar' : Spec k̄ ⟶ X` be geometric points of `X` lying over
`ȷ̄ : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, and let `η : fiberFunctor xbar' ⟶ fiberFunctor xbar`. Then `η`

of a finite étale `g : Y ⟶ Spec k` (via `p : Z ⟶ Y`), the map induced by `η` on the fiber
`{y : Spec k̄ ⟶ Y // y ≫ g = ȷ̄}` of `Y` at `ȷ̄` is the action of `σ` (precomposition with
`galSpec σ`).

`π₁(X, xbar) → π₁(Spec k, ȷ̄) = Gal(k̄/k)` induced by `f` is `σ`. -/
def LiesOver {xbar xbar' : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X}
    (η : fiberFunctor xbar' ⟶ fiberFunctor xbar) (σ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsFinite g] [IsEtale g] (Z : FiniteEtale X)
    (p : Z.left ⟶ Y), IsPullback p Z.hom g f →
    ∀ z : (fiberFunctor xbar').obj Z, ((η.app Z z).1 ≫ p) = galSpec σ ≫ z.1 ≫ p

/-- The identity lies over `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem liesOver_id (xbar : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X) :
    LiesOver f (𝟙 (fiberFunctor xbar)) 1 := by
  intro Y g _ _ Z p _ z
  simp [galSpec_one]

/-- If `η` lies over `σ` and `η'` lies over `τ`, then `η ≫ η'` lies over `τ * σ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem liesOver_comp {xbar xbar' xbar'' : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X}
    {η : fiberFunctor xbar'' ⟶ fiberFunctor xbar'}
    {η' : fiberFunctor xbar' ⟶ fiberFunctor xbar}
    {σ τ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k} (hη : LiesOver f η σ) (hη' : LiesOver f η' τ) :
    LiesOver f (η ≫ η') (τ * σ) := by
  intro Y g _ _ Z p hp z
  rw [NatTrans.comp_app, types_comp_apply, hη' Y g Z p hp, hη Y g Z p hp, galSpec_mul,
    Category.assoc]

/-- The `k`-rational points of `X`, i.e. the sections of `f : X ⟶ Spec k`. -/
def RationalPoint : Type u := { x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X // (x ≫ f) = 𝟙 _ }

/-- The section `Gal(k̄/k) → π₁(X, x ∘ ȷ̄)` induced by a `k`-point `x : Spec k ⟶ X` of `X`,
at the tautological geometric point `x ∘ ȷ̄` (where `ȷ̄ : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`): an element
`σ` acts on lifts `Spec k̄ ⟶ Y` of `x ∘ ȷ̄` by precomposition with `galSpec σ`. -/
noncomputable def rationalPointSection (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) :
    Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k →* etaleFundamentalGroup (specAlgebraicClosure k ≫ x) where
  toFun σ := NatIso.ofComponents (fun Z => Equiv.toIso
    { toFun := fun z => ⟨galSpec σ ≫ z.1, by
        rw [Category.assoc, z.2, ← Category.assoc, galSpec_comp_specAlgebraicClosure]⟩
      invFun := fun z => ⟨galSpec σ⁻¹ ≫ z.1, by
        rw [Category.assoc, z.2, ← Category.assoc, galSpec_comp_specAlgebraicClosure]⟩
      left_inv := fun z => Subtype.ext <| by
        simp only [← Category.assoc, ← galSpec_mul, inv_mul_cancel, galSpec_one,
          Category.id_comp]
      right_inv := fun z => Subtype.ext <| by
        simp only [← Category.assoc, ← galSpec_mul, mul_inv_cancel, galSpec_one,
          Category.id_comp] })
    (fun {Z Z'} h => by
      ext z
      simp [fiberFunctor])
  map_one' := Aut.ext <| NatTrans.ext <| funext fun Z => funext fun z => Subtype.ext <| by
    simp [galSpec_one]
    rfl
  map_mul' σ τ := Aut.ext <| NatTrans.ext <| funext fun Z => funext fun z => Subtype.ext <| by
    simp [galSpec_mul, Aut.Aut_mul_def]

/-- The homomorphism induced by a rational point is a section: `rationalPointSection x σ`
lies over `σ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem liesOver_rationalPointSection (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (σ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) :
    LiesOver f (rationalPointSection x σ).hom σ := by
  intro Y g _ _ Z p _ z
  simp [rationalPointSection]

/-- A homomorphism `s : Gal(k̄/k) →* π₁(X, xbar)` *is induced by* the `k`-point
`x : Spec k ⟶ X` if `s` is obtained from the section
`rationalPointSection x : Gal(k̄/k) →* π₁(X, x ∘ ȷ̄)` by transport of structure along a path
`γ : fiberFunctor (x ∘ ȷ̄) ≅ fiberFunctor xbar` lying over `k` (that is, inducing the identity
on the fibers of covers pulled back from `Spec k`).

Such paths form a torsor under `ker(π₁(X, xbar) → Gal(k̄/k)) = π₁(X_k̄, xbar)`, so the
homomorphisms induced by `x` form exactly the `π₁(X_k̄, xbar)`-conjugacy class of sections
attached to `x`. -/
def IsInducedBy (xbar : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X)
    (s : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k →* etaleFundamentalGroup xbar)
    (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : fiberFunctor (specAlgebraicClosure k ≫ x) ≅ fiberFunctor xbar,
    LiesOver f γ.hom 1 ∧ ∀ σ, s σ = γ.symm ≪≫ rationalPointSection x σ ≪≫ γ

/-- The tautological section attached to a rational point `x` is induced by `x`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isInducedBy_rationalPointSection (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) :
    IsInducedBy f (specAlgebraicClosure k ≫ x) (rationalPointSection x) x :=
  ⟨Iso.refl _, liesOver_id f _, fun σ => by simp⟩

end GaloisGroup

section Genus

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- The ring of sections `Γ(X, U)`, regarded as a `k`-algebra via `f : X ⟶ Spec k`. -/
def Sections (_f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (U : X.Opens) : Type u := Γ(X, U)

variable (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))

instance (U : X.Opens) : CommRing (Sections f U) := inferInstanceAs (CommRing Γ(X, U))

/-- The structure map `k → Γ(X, U)` induced by `f`. -/
noncomputable def toSections (U : X.Opens) : k →+* Sections f U :=
  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op).hom

noncomputable instance (U : X.Opens) : Algebra k (Sections f U) := (toSections f U).toAlgebra

/-- The restriction map `Γ(X, U) → Γ(X, V)` for `V ≤ U`. -/
def restriction {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) : Sections f U →+* Sections f V :=
  (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom

/-- The restriction maps are `k`-algebra homomorphisms. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem restriction_comp_toSections {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    (restriction f h).comp (toSections f U) = toSections f V := by
  simp only [restriction, toSections]
  rw [← CommRingCat.hom_comp, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]
  rfl

/-- For `V ≤ U`, `Γ(X, V)` is a `Γ(X, U)`-algebra compatibly with the `k`-algebra structures. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isScalarTower {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    letI := (restriction f h).toAlgebra
    IsScalarTower k (Sections f U) (Sections f V) := by
  letI := (restriction f h).toAlgebra
  exact IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun c =>
    (RingHom.congr_fun (restriction_comp_toSections f h) c).symm

/-- The `k`-vector space `H⁰(X, Ω¹_{X/k})` of global sections of the sheaf of relative
differentials of `X` over `k`: families of Kähler differentials `ω U ∈ Ω[Γ(X, U)⁄k]`,
indexed by the affine opens `U` of `X`, compatible with restriction. (Since the affine opens
form a basis of the topology of `X` and `Ω¹_{X/k}` restricted to an affine open `U` is the
quasi-coherent sheaf associated to `Ω[Γ(X, U)⁄k]`, this is the space of global sections of
`Ω¹_{X/k}`.) -/
noncomputable def globalDifferentials :
    Submodule k (∀ U : X.affineOpens, Ω[Sections f U.1⁄k]) where
  carrier := { ω | ∀ (U V : X.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ U.1),
    letI := (restriction f h).toAlgebra
    haveI := isScalarTower f h
    KaehlerDifferential.map k k (Sections f U.1) (Sections f V.1) (ω U) = ω V }
  zero_mem' := by
    intro U V h
    simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro ω ω' hω hω' U V h
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, map_add]
    rw [hω U V h, hω' U V h]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c ω hω U V h
    letI := (restriction f h).toAlgebra
    haveI := isScalarTower f h
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply]
    rw [← hω U V h, LinearMap.map_smul_of_tower]

/-- The genus of a smooth proper geometrically connected curve `X` over `k`:
the dimension over `k` of `H⁰(X, Ω¹_{X/k})`. -/
noncomputable def genus : ℕ := Module.finrank k (globalDifferentials f)

end Genus

/-- **Section conjecture** (Grothendieck, 1983).

Let $k$ be a field finitely generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $X$ be a complete (proper) smooth
geometrically connected curve of genus at least $2$ over $k$. Fix a geometric point
$\bar{x} \colon \mathrm{Spec}(\bar{k}) \to X$ lying over
$\bar{\jmath} \colon \mathrm{Spec}(\bar{k}) \to \mathrm{Spec}(k)$. Then every continuous section
$s$ of the homomorphism $\pi_1(X, \bar{x}) \to \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{k}/k)$ induced by the structure
map $X \to \mathrm{Spec}(k)$ is induced by a unique rational point $x \in X(k)$, i.e. $s$ is
$\pi_1(X_{\bar{k}}, \bar{x})$-conjugate to the section attached to $x$ for exactly one
$x \in X(k)$. Equivalently, the map from $X(k)$ to the set of continuous sections modulo
conjugation by the geometric fundamental group $\pi_1(X_{\bar{k}}, \bar{x})$ is a bijection. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem section_conjecture {k : Type u} [Field k] [CharZero k]
    (hk : (⊤ : IntermediateField ℚ k).FG)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f]
    [ConnectedSpace (pullback f (specAlgebraicClosure k) : Scheme.{u})] (hg : 2 ≤ genus f)
    (xbar : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k)) ⟶ X) (hxbar : (xbar ≫ f) = specAlgebraicClosure k)
    (s : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k →* etaleFundamentalGroup xbar) (hs : Continuous s)
    (hsec : ∀ σ, LiesOver f (s σ).hom σ) :
    ∃! x : RationalPoint f, IsInducedBy f xbar s x.1 := by
  sorry

end SectionConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the statement, and the notes correctly identify the hypotheses (genus ≥ 2, k finitely generated over ℚ, quotient by geometric-fundamental-group conjugacy) that the list entry omits and the article supplies. The only additional hypothesis I used beyond the notes is geometric connectedness of X, which is part of the standard meaning of "curve" in this conjecture and is needed for the statement to make sense.
modeling_decisions: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation (genus ≥ 2, k finitely generated over ℚ, sections modulo conjugation by the geometric fundamental group, bijectivity of X(k) → sections/conjugacy) is taken from the Wikipedia article and Grothendieck's letter, as the decomposition table's notes prescribe.

"Complete smooth curve" is rendered as `IsProper f` and `IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f` together with geometric connectedness `ConnectedSpace (pullback f (specAlgebraicClosure k))`. Geometric connectedness is not literally in the list entry, but it is part of the standard meaning of "curve" in the section conjecture (Grothendieck, Stix) and is needed for π₁(X) → Gal(k) to be the surjection of the fundamental exact sequence.

"Finitely generated over ℚ" is `[CharZero k]` plus `(⊤ : IntermediateField ℚ k).FG`, i.e. k is a finitely generated field extension of ℚ (not `Algebra.FiniteType`, which would force k to be a number field).

Gal(k) is `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k = Aut(k̄/k)` with Mathlib's Krull topology, k̄ = `AlgebraicClosure k` (equal to the separable closure since char 0). Geometric points are morphisms `Spec k̄ ⟶ X`; the theorem quantifies over all geometric points lying over ȷ̄ = `specAlgebraicClosure k` (the conjecture is base-point independent).

The étale fundamental group is `Aut (fiberFunctor xbar)` where `fiberFunctor` is Type-valued (fibers are sets of lifts of xbar to finite étale covers); no finiteness proof is needed for the statement. Its topology is the topology induced from ∏_Y (F(Y) → F(Y)) with each fiber discrete; since fibers of finite étale covers are finite, this is the usual profinite topology, and `Continuous s` is the usual continuity requirement on sections.

The homomorphism p : π₁(X, xbar) → Gal(k) is not constructed as a function (this would need the theorem Aut(F_ȷ̄) ≅ Gal(k)); instead the relation `LiesOver f η σ` ("p(η) = σ") is defined directly: η acts on the fiber of every cover Z → X that is a pullback (`IsPullback`) of a finite étale Y → Spec k as σ does on the fiber of Y at ȷ̄ (left action by precomposition with `galSpec σ = Spec.map σ`). API lemmas `liesOver_id`, `liesOver_comp`, `liesOver_rationalPointSection` check this behaves as a homomorphism and that rational points give sections.

The quotient by conjugation under π₁(X_k̄, xbar) is encoded in `IsInducedBy f xbar s x`: s equals the conjugate of the tautological section `rationalPointSection x : Gal(k) →* π₁(X, x ∘ ȷ̄)` by some path γ : F_{x∘ȷ̄} ≅ F_xbar lying over k (`LiesOver f γ.hom 1`). Paths over k form a torsor under ker p, which equals (the image of) π₁(X_k̄, xbar) by the fundamental exact sequence, so `IsInducedBy f xbar · x` is exactly the conjugacy class of sections attached to x, and `∃! x, IsInducedBy f xbar s x.1` for all sections s is equivalent to bijectivity of X(k) → sections/conjugacy.

The genus is defined as `Module.finrank k` of H⁰(X, Ω¹_{X/k}), realised as compatible families of Kähler differentials `Ω[Γ(X, U)⁄k]` over the affine opens U of X (affine opens form a basis; Ω¹ restricted to an affine open is the tilde of the Kähler module). For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve this is the genus. `finrank` is 0 for infinite-dimensional spaces, which cannot occur for proper X.

The repository's global asymptotics notation `f ≫ g` clashes with categorical composition; compositions appearing on the left of `=` are parenthesized so the categorical parse is selected. This is purely syntactic.
Rational points are `RationalPoint f = {x : Spec k ⟶ X // x ≫ f = 𝟙}`. AMS tags 11 (number theory) and 14 (algebraic geometry) were chosen.
